Smt. Chandresh vs Gulab Singh on 7 April, 2025

 In The High Court Of Madhya Pradesh

High Court Of Madhya Pradesh

sentences.text:
Before
 Hon'Ble Shri Justice Ashish Shroti

On The 7 th Of April, 2025
 Misc. Appeal No. 4981 of 2019
 Smt. Chandresh And Others
 Versus
 Gulab Singh And Others
 Appearance:
 Shri Bhagwan Das Verma - learned counsel for the appell
 Shri Nirendra Singh Tomar- learned counsel for responde
 Order

1 . The appellants have filed this appeal under Section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act being dissatisfied with the amount of compensation awarded by the 17th Additional Motor Accident Claims Tribunal vide impugned award dated 27/06/2019 passed in Claim Case No.130/2015.

2. The facts necessary for decision of the case are that on 29/09/2014, the deceased- Arjun alongwith his brother-Karan was sleeping in the house and at around 12:00 in the night, the offending truck bearing registration No. RJ-11-GA-1589 dashed their house on account of rash and negligent driving by non-applicant no.2.
Arjun as well as his brother, Karan, suffered serious injuries because of the aforesaid accident and resultantly both expired.
The offending vehicle was owned by non-applicant no.2 while it was insured with non-applicant no.3.
Separate claim petitions were filed by the appellants in respect of the death of Arjun as well as Karan.

In this appeal,
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-GWL:8168 2 MA-4981-2019 we are concerned with the award passed in respect of death of Arjun.
3. It is now not in dispute that the deceased- Arjun was aged about 15 years on the date of accident.
The findings with regard to rash and negligent driving by non-applicant no.1 and the death of Arjun on account of the accident occurred on 29/09/2014 are also not challenged.
Insurance Company has also not challenged the finding with regard to its liability to pay the compensation.
Thus, in the instant appeal, we are concerned only with regard to the quantum of compensation payable to the appellants on account of death of Arjun.

4 . Since the deceased was minor on the date of accident, learned Claims Tribunal has taken notional income of Rs.30,000/- per annum and has applied multiplier of 15 based upon the age of his parents.

The amount of Rs.15,000/- towards loss of estate, Rs.40,000/- towards loss of love and Smt. Chandresh vs Gulab Singh on 7 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/144837970/
1 affection and Rs.15000/- towards funeral expenses has been awarded by Tribunal.

entities.text: Chandresh vs Gulab Singh on 7 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Further an amount of Rs.80,000/- has been awarded towards damage caused to their house because of accident.

5 . Learned counsel for the appellants submitted that the Claims Tribunal erred in taking notional income of Rs.30,000/- per annum instead of assessing income based upon the minimum wages payable to an unskilled workman.
He further submits that Claims Tribunal erred in taking multiplier based upon the parents age.
It is his submission that the multiplier of 18 based upon the age of the deceased ought to have been applied.
He further submits that Tribunal erred in not awarding any amount towards future prospect.
He thus, prays for enhancement of compensation after NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-GWL:8168 3 MA-4981-2019 calculating the same in accordance with the aforesaid submissions.

6 . Learned counsel for the respondent/Insurance Company opposes the prayer and submits that since the deceased was minor, income cannot be assessed based upon the minimum wages and Tribunal is justified in taking notional income of Rs.30,000/- per annum.

He further submits that as per the judgment rendered by the Apex Court in the case of Sarla Verma (Smt.) and Ors. Vs. Delhi Transport Corporation and Anr. reported in (2009) 6 SCC 121, multiplier of 15 is applicable even on the basis of age of minor deceased.

entities.text: Sarla Verma (Smt.) and Ors. Vs. Delhi Transport Corporation and Anr. reported in (2009) 6 SCC 121
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Therefore, he submits that the multiplier applied by the Tribunal is correct.

The learned counsel for respondent/Insurance Company further submits that there is no evidence led by the appellants for assessing the damage caused to the house and therefore, the compensation awarded by the Tribunal towards damage to the house is adequate and does not call for any interference.
He, thus, prays for dismissal of the appeal.
7. Considered the arguments and perused the record.
8 . Learned counsel for the appellants submitted that income of the deceased be assessed on the basis of minimum wages.
However, he could not support his argument with any legal provision.

On the other hand, the Apex Court in the case of Kurvan Ansari Alias Kurvan Ali and another Vs. Shyam Kishore Murmu and another reported in (2022)1 SCC 317 has held that income of the deceased minor is to be taken on notional basis.

entities.text: Kurvan Ansari Alias Kurvan Ali and another Vs. Shyam Kishore Murmu and another reported in (2022)1 SCC 317
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Thus, income of the deceased taken to be Rs.30,000/- per annum in this case is just and proper.

Further, as per the judgment of the Apex Court in the case of Sarla Verma (supra) , even if age of the deceased is to be taken into account, NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-GWL:8168 4 MA-4981-2019 multiplier of 15 is to be applied.
Thus, on this count also appellants do not get any benefit.

9. In the case of Smt. Chhoti Devi & Ors. Vs. Smt. Sharda Devi & Ors. passed in M.A. No.523/2015 decided on 11/10/2018, the coordinate bench of this Court has held that future prospects @ 40% is to be applied in the case of minor.

entities.text: Smt. Chhoti Devi & Ors. Vs. Smt. Sharda Devi & Ors
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Thus, compensation is liable to be enhanced under this head.
Thus, taking notional income of Rs.30,000/- enhanced by 40% towards future prospects and applying the multiplier of 15, the total compensation under these heads comes to Rs.6,30,000/-.
A sum of Rs.73,000/- is payable towards other conventional heads.
Thus, the the total amount of compensation comes to Rs.7,05,000/-.
The learned Claims Tribunal has already awarded Rs.5,20,000/-.

Thus, after adjusting the amount of compensation awarded by Claims Tribunal, the appellants are held entitled to enhancement of Rs.1,85,000/- which will be payable to them Smt. Chandresh vs Gulab Singh on 7 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/144837970/
2

alongwith interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of filing of claim petition i.e.
21/11/2014.
10.
The appeal is allowed and disposed off in aforesaid terms.

(ASHISH SHROTI) JUDGE rahul Smt. Chandresh vs Gulab Singh on 7 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/144837970/
